events.title: First Hot Air Balloon Passenger Flight with Animals
events.description: At Versailles, the Montgolfier brothers launched a hot air balloon carrying a sheep, a duck, and a rooster before King Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette, and a large crowd. The balloon flew for about eight minutes and landed safely roughly two miles away.
events.significance: The flight showed that living creatures could survive at altitude, paving the way for the first human aerial flight in November 1783 and the development of aviation.

events.title: George Washington's Farewell Address Published
events.description: President George Washington's Farewell Address was published in Claypoole's American Daily Advertiser in Philadelphia. In it he announced he would not seek a third term and warned against permanent foreign alliances and bitter political partisanship.
events.significance: By stepping down voluntarily, Washington set the two-term precedent for the American presidency, and the address became a foundational statement of early American political thought and foreign policy.

events.title: Death of President James A. Garfield
events.description: James A. Garfield, the 20th U.S. president, died from complications of wounds inflicted by assassin Charles Guiteau in July 1881. He had served only about six and a half months in office, and Vice President Chester A. Arthur succeeded him.
events.significance: Garfield's assassination fueled public demand for civil service reform, leading to the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act of 1883, which established merit-based federal hiring.

events.title: Mexico City Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck Mexico City early in the morning, with a major aftershock the following day. Hundreds of buildings collapsed, and estimates of the death toll range from about 5,000 to over 10,000 people.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest disasters in Mexico's history, prompting major reforms in building codes and emergency preparedness and spurring the growth of civil society organizing in the country.

events.title: Thai Military Coup
events.description: The Thai military, led by General Sondhi Boonyaratglin, seized power while Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra was abroad at the United Nations. The army declared martial law, abolished the constitution, and dissolved parliament.
events.significance: It was Thailand's first coup in 15 years and began a long period of political polarization and instability marked by recurring protests, court rulings, and further military intervention.
